title: Underwater Momentum Transfer Lab
description: An underwater physics lab where the user launches a damaged space helmet along a frictionless track toward a floating fish, experimenting with elastic and inelastic collisions. Users adjust the helmet's mass and velocity, toggle collision type, and observe conservation of momentum and kinetic energy in real time, with full undo/redo support for each parameter change.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load DamagedHelmet.glb and BarramundiFish.glb. Scene: an underwater environment with blue-green fog, a subtle caustic light pattern on a flat plane acting as the track floor, and ambient plus directional lighting. Place the helmet on the left side of the track and the fish on the right, both resting on the plane. UI panel (HTML overlay) with: (1) helmet mass slider 1-10 kg, (2) fish mass slider 1-10 kg, (3) helmet initial velocity slider 1-20 m/s, (4) collision type toggle: elastic vs perfectly inelastic, (5) a Launch button, (6) a Reset button, (7) Undo and Redo buttons for all parameter changes. Implement a history stack that records every slider or toggle change so Undo reverts the last parameter modification and Redo re-applies it. On Launch, animate the helmet sliding right toward the fish using requestAnimationFrame. On collision contact, compute final velocities using conservation of momentum (and kinetic energy for elastic mode). For inelastic mode the objects stick together and move as one. Display a live HUD showing total momentum and total kinetic energy before and after collision, highlighting conservation. After collision, objects continue moving at computed velocities until they leave the visible track, then auto-stop. Reset returns objects to start positions. Camera: perspective at 45 degrees above and in front, OrbitControls enabled. The fish should have a gentle idle bobbing animation. Add particle bubbles on collision impact. Ensure at least 10 distinct interaction steps are needed: adjust helmet mass, adjust fish mass, adjust velocity, toggle collision type, launch, observe, reset, undo a parameter, redo it, relaunch with new settings. All physics calculations must be shown numerically on the HUD.
